heading: INT. FARMHOUSE-STYLE KITCHEN, SUBURBAN HOME - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FARMHOUSE-STYLE KITCHEN, SUBURBAN HOME - NIGHT
The lights went out an hour ago and the house has not yet decided whether to be afraid.
Candles, mismatched, stand on the Formica.
Wind pulls at the storm door.
Somewhere on the street a transformer pops, and the dark swallows the hum of the refrigerator whole.
A woman in her thirties, THE WOMAN, stands at the sink in a quilted robe, scrubbing a pot that is already clean.
Her husband, GERALD FINCH, forty, sits at the table, his tie loosened, pretending to read a seed catalogue by candlelight.
At the far end, ruffling a pack of cards with great concentration, is his mother, OLIVE, seventy.
Two children, TEDDY, 12, and ROSIE, 8, sit cross-legged on the linoleum, whispering over a flashlight.
The sixth, a neighbour, DOT WALLACE, fifties, in a headscarf and curlers, has arrived to borrow a candle and stayed.
The wall phone rings.
Everyone freezes.
It is the only thing in the house with power.
I'll get it.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: She lifts the receiver.
A man's voice, thin and fast, fills the kitchen.
Eleanor? It's Frank. Is Gerald there? Tell him the hospital called.
units.name: CALLER

units.text: The Woman, who is named Eleanor, turns the receiver away from her chest.
Gerald does not look up from the catalogue.
The page has not turned in twenty minutes.
Who was it?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Frank.
units.name: ELEANOR

units.text: Don't you tell him yet.
units.name: OLIVE

units.text: Oh, Eleanor, don't.
units.name: DOT

units.text: ON PHONE: a pencilled note in the margin of the telephone pad, in Gerald's handwriting: "Tues.
3pm.
Dr. Prentiss."
Eleanor sets the receiver on the counter.
Teddy lowers the flashlight.
Rosie, who is eight and misses nothing, takes her brother's hand.
The wind rattles the door again.
In the little light, Gerald folds the catalogue shut, very precisely, and lays his palm flat on its cover as if to hold it down.
Put the kettle on, love. The gas still works.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: She does.
The flame blooms blue, enormous, the brightest thing in the house.
